title: Power: How you get it, how it can change you, with Dacher Keltner, PhD

sentences.en: Power is one of those terms that we all think we understand.
sentences.zh: “权力”是我们自以为理解的词汇之一。

sentences.en: It's being in a position to call the shots, to set the agenda, to lead others and maybe to boss them around or even punish them, right?
sentences.zh: 它意味着处于能发号施令、制定议程、领导他人，甚至颐指气使乃至惩罚他人的位置，对吧？

sentences.en: Our culture's understanding of power has been heavily shaped by one person,
sentences.zh: 我们文化中对权力的理解，在很大程度上受到一个人的影响，

sentences.en: Niccolò Machiavelli, the Renaissance era politician and diplomat, who infamously wrote that power is essentially about force, fraud, ruthlessness, and strategic violence.
sentences.zh: 那就是尼科洛·马基雅维利，这位文艺复兴时期的政治家和外交官，他臭名昭著地写道，权力的本质就是武力、欺诈、冷酷和战略性的暴力。

sentences.en: But what if he was wrong?
sentences.zh: 但如果他错了呢？

sentences.en: So what is power?
sentences.zh: 那么，什么是权力？

sentences.en: Why do people seek it?
sentences.zh: 为什么人们追求权力？

sentences.en: What types of people seek it?
sentences.zh: 什么样的人会追求权力？

sentences.en: And if you want power, what's the best way to get it?
sentences.zh: 如果你想要权力，获得它的最佳途径是什么？

sentences.en: Is it human nature to abuse power?
sentences.zh: 滥用权力是人性使然吗？

sentences.en: And why do some people lust for it?
sentences.zh: 为什么有些人对权力如此渴望？

sentences.en: What is the impact of powerlessness?
sentences.zh: 无权无势会带来什么影响？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: Our guest today is Dr. Dacher Keltner, founding director of the Greater Good Science Center and psychology professor at the University of California, Berkeley.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的嘉宾是达彻·凯尔特纳博士，他是至善科学中心创始主任，也是加州大学伯克利分校的心理学教授。

sentences.en: He is author of the bestselling book,
sentences.zh: 他著有畅销书《权力悖论：我们如何获得与失去影响力》，

sentences.en: The Power Paradox, How We Gain and Lose Influence, as well as host of the podcast,
sentences.zh: 同时也是播客《幸福科学》的主持人，这也是他共同教授的一门热门课程的名字。

sentences.en: The Science of Happiness, which is also the name of a popular course that he co-instructs.
sentences.zh: 权力是他研究的众多领域之一，此外还有爱、同情心、美、社会阶层、不平等和敬畏感。

sentences.en: Power is one of the many areas he studies along with love, compassion, beauty, social class, inequality, and awe.
sentences.zh: 感谢您今天参加我们的节目，凯尔特纳博士。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us today, Dr. Keltner.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能和你在一起，金。

sentences.en: It's great to be with you, Kim.
sentences.zh: 在《心理学谈话》中，我们通常从定义术语开始。

sentences.en: Here at Speaking of Psychology, we often start by defining terMs.
sentences.zh: 我在开场白中问过这个问题：什么是权力？

sentences.en: And I asked this question in the introduction, what is power?
sentences.zh: 你是如何定义的？

sentences.en: How do you define it?
sentences.zh: 你的定义与马基雅维利的有何不同？

sentences.en: And is your definition different from Machiavelli's?
sentences.zh: 是的，你知道，这被证明是权力科学中最难做的事情之一。

sentences.en: Yeah, you know, this turns out to be one of the hardest things to do in the science of power.
sentences.zh: 伟大的哲学家伯特兰·罗素曾写道，权力是社会生活的基本媒介。

sentences.en: You know, Bertrand Russell, the great philosopher, wrote that power is the basic medium of social life.
sentences.zh: 我和同事研究权力已有25年，我倾向于同意这一点，它无处不在。

sentences.en: And as I've studied power with my colleagues for 25 years, I tend to agree, it's just everywhere.
sentences.zh: 这使得它很难定义。

sentences.en: And that makes it hard to define.
sentences.zh: 我们确实与一位名叫斯蒂芬·卢克斯的人保持一致，他关于权力的论述非常精彩。

sentences.en: And we really align, and there are various definitions of it, but we really align with somebody named Stephen Lukes, who has a wonderful treatment of power.
sentences.zh: 他是一位社会学家，他认为权力是你改变他人状态或影响他人的能力，对吧？

sentences.en: He's a sociologist, that power is your capacity to alter the states of other people or to influence others, right?
sentences.zh: 所以权力不同于地位——卡梅隆·安德森研究过这个课题——地位是你从同龄人、同事和周围人那里获得的尊重。

sentences.en: So power is different from status, which Cameron Anderson has studied, which is the respect you get from your peers and your colleagues and the people around you.
sentences.zh: 权力不同于财富和阶级。

sentences.en: Power is different than wealth and class.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在我们的研究中，这两个概念的相关性仅在0.15到0.2之间。

sentences.en: And in fact, in our work, those two constructs only correlate about 0.15, 0.2.
sentences.zh: 权力不同于支配，支配是指强迫他人服从或操纵他人的策略。

sentences.en: Power is different from dominance, which is strategies to coerce people to manipulate.
sentences.zh: 权力是你影响和改变周围人心智状态的能力。

sentences.en: Power is your capacity to influence and alter the states of mind of people around you.
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么有些人追求权力？

sentences.en: And perhaps that's why more extroverted people gravitate to positions of power and want it, and people who are a little bit quieter,

sentences.en: So I think part of the reason that people shy away from it is the attention that is forced upon you once you have power.

sentences.zh: 说到拥有巨大的权力，有一句古老的格言说“绝对的权力导致绝对的腐败”，或者说“权力导致腐败，绝对的权力导致绝对的腐败”。

sentences.zh: 这是一个人的例子，他通过汉娜·阿伦特所说的方式让我们感到惊讶，即通过接触网络并激励他们来获得权力。

sentences.en: And then I found myself losing touch.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: And I think you could look at the last presidency is a textbook case.
sentences.zh: 他与人们对话。

sentences.en: Example of somebody who caught us by surprise by, as Hannah Arendt says, like gaining your power by reaching a network and inspiring them.
sentences.zh: 然后是他行事的方式。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 以及新冠疫情带来的后果，我们作为一个文化体的失败，说明了当我们不认真对待权力并滥用它时会发生什么。

sentences.en: He spoke to people.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你在《权力悖论》一书中确实谈到了很多关于你在KO Drive长大后，对相对无权无势的理解。

sentences.en: And then the way that he conducted himself.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And then the fallout of COVID is, and our, our failure as a culture speaks to what happens when we don't take power seriously and we abuse it.
sentences.zh: 你那里的很多邻居相对来说都没有权力，这对他们的生活轨迹产生了一些可观察到的影响。

sentences.en: Well, you do talk quite a bit in your book, the power paradox about what you learned regarding relative powerlessness as a result of growing up on KO drive.
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈这一点，以及你从中真正学到了什么吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: And a lot of your neighbors there were relatively powerless and they had some observable effects on, on their life trajectories.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你的提问，你知道，

sentences.en: Can you talk about that and really what you learned from that?
sentences.zh: 是的，

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 是的，

sentences.en: Thanks for asking that, you know,
sentences.zh: 是的，

sentences.en: yeah,
sentences.zh: 是的

sentences.en: Kim, I was, it was really interesting.
sentences.zh: Kim，我当时，那真的很有趣。

sentences.en: My mom was a professor at a state university and a feminist and,
sentences.zh: 我母亲曾是一所州立大学的教授，也是一位女权主义者，而且，

sentences.en: and she and my dad, we went from a very strong middle-class community where the schools were good.
sentences.zh: 她和我父亲，我们从一个非常稳固的中产阶级社区搬走，那里的学校条件很好。

sentences.en: And the kids became psychologists and teachers and medical doctors and the like.
sentences.zh: 孩子们后来都成了心理学家、教师、医生之类的人。

sentences.en: And we moved for various reasons to the poor rural foothills of the Sierras in
sentences.zh: 出于各种原因，我们搬到了加利福尼亚州内华达山脉脚下贫穷的农村地区，

sentences.en: California.
sentences.zh: 加利福尼亚州。

sentences.en: And, and our town had 300 people.
sentences.zh: 我们的镇上只有300人。

sentences.en: And we lived on a street.
sentences.zh: 我们住在一条街上。

sentences.en: There were 19 kids on the street.
sentences.zh: 那条街上有19个孩子。

sentences.en: I think only three went to college.
sentences.zh: 我想只有三个上了大学。

sentences.en: Two were my brother and me.
sentences.zh: 其中两个是我哥哥和我。

sentences.en: And then a third was my friend memo who went to college because of my parents who really encouraged him to.
sentences.zh: 第三个是我的朋友Memo，他能上大学是因为我父母真的鼓励他去。

sentences.en: So it was, it was very poor and rural poor.
sentences.zh: 所以那里非常贫穷，是农村的那种贫穷。

sentences.en: And as I was writing the last chapter of the power paradox, I think when we think about power, we have to, it's tempting to only think about the abuse of power,
sentences.zh: 当我在写《权力悖论》的最后一章时，我想当我们思考权力时，我们必须——只去想权力的滥用是很诱人的，

sentences.en: but you really have to think about this collective process of power.
sentences.zh: 但你真的必须思考这种权力的集体过程。

sentences.en: What happens to the people who, who are not given a chance at having power and influence in society, right?
sentences.zh: 那些在社会中没有机会获得权力和影响力的人会怎样，对吧？

sentences.en: The disenfranchised, the poor.
sentences.zh: 那些被剥夺权利的人，穷人。

sentences.en: And I was growing up around them.
sentences.zh: 我就是在他们身边长大的。

sentences.en: And I was really struck by the work of people like Keely Muscatel,
sentences.zh: 我真的被Keely Muscatel、

sentences.en: Edith Chen and Greg Miller,
sentences.zh: Edith Chen和Greg Miller、

sentences.en: Shelly Taylor and others on, wow, what happens if you're not included in society and you don't have a voice?
sentences.zh: Shelly Taylor等人的研究深深打动了，哇，如果你被社会排斥，没有话语权，会发生什么？

sentences.en: And we started, people started to learn high cortisol stress,
sentences.zh: 我们开始，人们开始了解高皮质醇压力，

sentences.en: rejection regions of your brain, inflammation in your body, shortened life expectancy.
sentences.zh: 大脑中的排斥区域、身体炎症、预期寿命缩短。

sentences.en: Nancy Adler's groundbreaking paper from 1996, the lower you fall on a rung, a 10 rung ladder of status in society, the shorter you live.
sentences.zh: Nancy Adler 1996年的开创性论文指出，你在社会地位的10级阶梯上跌落得越低，你的寿命就越短。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And, and I started Kim to think as I was finishing the power paradox about the people I grew up around on KO drive.
sentences.zh: Kim，当我在完成《权力悖论》时，我开始想到我在KO大道上一起长大的那些人。

sentences.en: And they fit that profile, right?
sentences.zh: 他们符合那种状况，对吧？

sentences.en: They were great human beings.
sentences.zh: 他们都是很棒的人。

sentences.en: They would share anything with you.
sentences.zh: 他们愿意和你分享任何东西。

sentences.en: You always had a spot at their dinner table.
sentences.zh: 你的餐桌上总有他们的位置。

sentences.en: In some sense it was idyllic, right?
sentences.zh: 在某种意义上，那是田园诗般的，对吧？

sentences.en: And free.
sentences.zh: 而且自由。

sentences.en: But at the same time, people were dying younger, you know, they, they, and you could look at them and they, there was more depression.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，人们死得更早，你知道，他们，而且你可以看着他们，他们有更多的抑郁。

sentences.en: There was more clinical levels of anxiety, which we know to co-vary with lower resources.
sentences.zh: 有更多临床水平的焦虑，我们知道这与资源匮乏是共变的。

sentences.en: And as I thought about the people around me, there were people dying when they were 40, there were people dying in 60,
sentences.zh: 当我想到我周围的人时，有人40岁就去世了，有人60岁去世，

sentences.en: And so I thought, wow,
sentences.zh: 所以我心想，哇，

sentences.en: when I was 10 years old, I moved from this middle-class world and, and I moved to a poor rural country street lane.
sentences.zh: 我10岁时，从那个中产阶级世界搬到了这条贫穷的乡村小路上。

sentences.en: And it felt magical to me, but it had this.
sentences.zh: 对我来说这感觉很神奇，但它有这个。

sentences.en: Had a downside.
sentences.zh: 有不好的一面。

sentences.en: this sadness to it.
sentences.zh: 它有一种悲伤。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That was about power.
sentences.zh: 那关乎权力。

sentences.en: And what we, what happens when society doesn't give people a chance.
sentences.zh: 以及当社会不给人们机会时会发生什么。

sentences.en: Well, on the other side of the coin, then are people who have power, relatively speaking, doesn't have to be absolute power, but people who have power, are they healthier?
sentences.zh: 嗯，硬币的另一面是那些拥有权力的人，相对而言，不一定是绝对权力，但那些拥有权力的人，他们更健康吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: you know, this is,
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是，

sentences.en: I mean, we, we all, you know, there are abuses to power, there are costs to power.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们，我们都，你知道，权力有滥用，权力有代价。

sentences.en: We, we like to talk about how it's lonely at the top and, and there are interesting variations on that idea.
sentences.zh: 我们，我们喜欢谈论高处不胜寒，而且关于这个观点有各种有趣的变体。

sentences.en: But the raw facts of the matter are that if you have resources and you have power and voice, you, you feel better about life.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，如果你有资源，有权力和话语权，你，你对生活的感觉会更好。

sentences.en: You are happier about life.
sentences.zh: 你对生活会更快乐。

sentences.en: You feel greater joy in your work.
sentences.zh: 你在工作中会感到更大的快乐。

sentences.en: You are physically more robuSt.
sentences.zh: 你的身体更强健。

sentences.en: You have a longer life expectancy.
sentences.zh: 你的预期寿命更长。

sentences.en: Your kids will live longer, right?
sentences.zh: 你的孩子会活得更久，对吧？

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实是。

sentences.en: And, and that's, that was really interesting to me.
sentences.zh: 而且，那对我来说真的很有趣。

sentences.en: And it's to one of your questions earlier, which is that we want everybody around us to enjoy that sense of influence, right?
sentences.zh: 这涉及你之前提出的一个问题，即我们希望周围的每个人都能享受那种影响力，对吧？

sentences.en: And power because of these consequences or correlates of it.
sentences.zh: 以及因为这些后果或相关性而带来的权力。

sentences.en: And for people who are suspicious of power, want to eliminate it, they should really be thinking about this profile of greater robustness in mind and body.
sentences.zh: 对于那些对权力持怀疑态度、想要消除权力的人来说，他们真的应该考虑这种在身心上更强健的状况。

sentences.en: If you're, feel empowered in your context.
sentences.zh: 如果你在你的环境中感到被赋权。

sentences.en: In your work, you talk about how power is given.
sentences.zh: 在你的著作中，你谈到了权力是如何被赋予的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But we see situations every day where people gain power by force, whether they sabotage a coworker or they steal someone's spouse or even overthrow a government.
sentences.zh: 但我们每天都能看到人们通过武力获得权力的情况，无论是破坏同事的工作，还是抢走别人的配偶，甚至是推翻政府。

sentences.en: So are you saying that true power can never be rested or stolen?
sentences.zh: 所以你是说真正的权力永远不能被夺取或窃取吗？

sentences.en: Well, you know, this is the, this was a great observation of a sociologist who said, power is given to you.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，这是一位社会学家的伟大观察，他说，权力是赋予你的。

sentences.en: It's not taken.
sentences.zh: 它不是被夺走的。

sentences.en: And that's a direct confrontation with the Machiavellian view of all power is taken.
sentences.zh: 这与马基雅维利主义认为所有权力都是被夺取的观点直接对立。

sentences.en: And, and I think that the, and I think in many ways he, this observation of power is given reflects this interplay between your capacity to influence
sentences.zh: 而且，我认为，我认为在很多方面，他，这种关于权力被赋予的观察反映了你影响他人的能力，

sentences.en: and what other people think about your, your leadership and your power, your execution of power.
sentences.zh: 以及其他人对你的领导力、你的权力、你行使权力的看法之间的相互作用。

sentences.en: And in some sense, in a lot of contexts, it's given to you.
sentences.zh: 在某种意义上，在许多情况下，权力是赋予你的。

sentences.en: And that's the basis of enduring power is to lead and use power in a way that does not abuse.
sentences.zh: 这就是持久权力的基础，即以一种不滥用的方式去领导和行使权力。

sentences.en: We're looking right now at Andrew Cuomo who was, you know, literally today, you know,
sentences.zh: 我们现在正看着安德鲁·科莫，你知道，就在今天，你知道，

sentences.en: 16 months ago, he was the hero of the United States.
sentences.zh: 16个月前，他还是美国的英雄。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And now he's a, he's a disgrace because of how, because he, people are no longer giving him power.
sentences.zh: 而现在他是一个，他是一个耻辱，因为，因为人们不再赋予他权力了。

sentences.en: Those 11 women reporting on, on him are saying, we can't give this guy power anymore and he's going to lose his power.
sentences.zh: 那11名举报他的女性在说，我们不能再给这家伙权力了，他将失去他的权力。

sentences.en: So I think it's a very powerful dynamic in most relationships, but then you have to worry.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这在大多数关系中是一种非常有力的动态，但你必须担心。

sentences.en: And this is, you know, right now people are thinking a lot about authoritarianism.
sentences.zh: 这是，你知道，现在人们对威权主义思考了很多。

sentences.en: Like what are the conditions in which white supremacy or authoritarian, political authoritarianism can rise and, and return us to these asymmetric dynamics.
sentences.zh: 比如白人至上主义或政治威权主义在什么条件下会兴起，并让我们回到这些不对称的动态中。

sentences.en: And I think this is one of the key warning signs is when you no longer as a member of a community can give people power.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个关键的警告信号，即当你作为社区的一员不再能赋予人们权力时。

sentences.en: And Trump tried to degrade that.
sentences.zh: 特朗普试图削弱这一点。

sentences.en: Frankly, he tried to undermine accountability, undermine the scrutiny of his behavior, undermine the press whose job is to be, to give people power and to critique them.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，他试图破坏问责制，破坏对他行为的审查，破坏媒体，而媒体的工作就是赋予人们权力并批评他们。

sentences.en: And that's a warning sign of when power is healthy and when it's imbalanced.
sentences.zh: 这是权力何时健康、何时失衡的警告信号。

sentences.en: So it really depends on the context and how we negotiate power.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实取决于环境以及我们如何协商权力。

sentences.en: Funny that you should mention Andrew Cuomo, because I was going to ask a question about him.
sentences.zh: 提到安德鲁·科莫很有趣，因为我正想问关于他的问题。

sentences.en: And when I was a journalist, I covered his father who was the governor in New York and his father was a bully.
sentences.zh: 当我还是记者时，我报道过他的父亲，也就是纽约州州长，他父亲是个恶霸。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, he was a bully to journalists.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他对记者是个恶霸。

sentences.en: I'm sure he was a bully to other people.
sentences.zh: 我相信他对其他人也是个恶霸。

sentences.en: And I'm just wondering, like who teaches us these power styles as we grow up?
sentences.zh: 我只是想知道，我们成长过程中是谁教给我们这些权力风格的？

sentences.en: And I mean, you could even contrast say Andrew Cuomo with his brother, who seems like, you know, not the same kind of guy, but they grew up with the same dad.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你甚至可以将安德鲁·科莫与他的兄弟进行对比，他看起来，你知道，不是那种人，但他们是在同一个父亲身边长大的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, what do we know about how you learn your power style?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，关于如何学习权力风格，我们知道些什么？

sentences.en: We don't know.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道。

sentences.en: And that's a terrific question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个极好的问题。

sentences.en: And in fact,
sentences.zh: 事实上，

sentences.en: Leanne Tambrinke and I just published a paper in the Journal of Personality and Social Psychology on kind of these two models of power that you and I have been talking about,
sentences.zh: Leanne Tambrinke和我刚刚在《人格与社会心理学杂志》上发表了一篇论文，关于你我一直在讨论的这两种权力模型，

sentences.en: Kim, more collaborative model of power.
sentences.zh: Kim，更具协作性的权力模型。

sentences.en: Women tend to endorse that a little bit more, for example, versus a coercive domineering model of power.
sentences.zh: 例如，女性往往更倾向于支持这一点，而不是强制性的、专横的权力模型。

sentences.en: And so these are these theories of power that rise to different degrees in different cultures and historical moments and sectors of society.
sentences.zh: 所以这些是权力理论，在不同的文化、历史时刻和社会部门中以不同程度兴起。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So we know my hunch is, is the coercive model is more popular in Washington,
sentences.zh: 所以我们知道，我的直觉是，强制模型在华盛顿特区更受欢迎，

sentences.en: D.C.
sentences.zh: 特区。

sentences.en: and politics and so forth.
sentences.zh: 以及政治等等。

sentences.en: But, you know, the I think one of the really interesting findings in the science of power is, and there have been these large meta analyses of our model,
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我认为权力科学中一个非常有趣的发现是，并且已经有了关于我们模型的大型荟萃分析，

sentences.en: our thinking about power is changing.
sentences.zh: 我们对权力的思考正在改变。

sentences.en: And you referred to this at the start of, as a culture, we're always changing our views of power.
sentences.zh: 你在开头提到了这一点，作为一个文化，我们一直在改变对权力的看法。

sentences.en: 50 years ago, it was kind of the madman approach to power of like, dominate, men, you know, hierarchical.
sentences.zh: 50年前，那是一种疯狂的权力方式，比如统治、男性、你知道，等级制度。

sentences.en: And we've moved in lots of ways to a more, a different theory or approach to power, more collaborative.
sentences.zh: 我们在很多方面已经转向了一种不同的权力理论或方法，更具协作性。

sentences.en: I do a lot of work with medical doctors.
sentences.zh: 我与医生们做了很多工作。

sentences.en: 40 years ago, the medical doctor was more Machiavellian in executing power.
sentences.zh: 40年前，医生在行使权力时更马基雅维利主义。

sentences.en: And now it's much more collaborative.
sentences.zh: 而现在它更具协作性。

sentences.en: So it's always in flux.
sentences.zh: 所以它总是在变化中。

sentences.en: How do we get it from our families?
sentences.zh: 我们是如何从家庭中获得它的？

sentences.en: We don't know.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道。

sentences.en: It's a great question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: How do we get it as a function of culture?
sentences.zh: 我们是如何作为文化功能获得它的？

sentences.en: If I'm from a super touch oriented culture, does that get me into more trouble?
sentences.zh: 如果我来自一个超级注重身体接触的文化，这会让我陷入更多麻烦吗？

sentences.en: Like, you know, that may be the case.
sentences.zh: 比如，你知道，情况可能确实如此。

sentences.en: So that's a great question for future research.
sentences.zh: 所以这对未来的研究来说是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: Well, let's shift gears for a minute and talk about gossip, because I know you've looked at that as well.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们换个话题，谈谈流言蜚语，因为我知道你也研究过这个。

sentences.en: And what's the role of gossip relative to power and how has social media affected gossip and, by extension, its connection to power?
sentences.zh: 流言蜚语相对于权力的作用是什么？社交媒体如何影响了流言蜚语，进而影响了它与权力的联系？

sentences.en: What a terrific question.
sentences.zh: 真是个极好的问题。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: People always, when they hear I sing the praises of gossip, are like,
sentences.zh: 人们总是，当他们听到我赞美流言蜚语时，会觉得，

sentences.en: I'm going to go after that guy.
sentences.zh: 我要去对付那个人。

sentences.en: You know, so, you know, this came from a brilliant paper, my, our interest in gossip from, by Christopher Bum,
sentences.zh: 你知道，所以，你知道，这来自一篇精彩的论文，我们对流言蜚语的兴趣来自Christopher Bum，

sentences.en: who's an anthropologiSt.
sentences.zh: 他是一位人类学家。

sentences.en: And it was a prize winning paper, I think from 1991, where he studied 4,800 gatherer societies.
sentences.zh: 那是一篇获奖论文，我想是1991年的，他研究了4800个采集者社会。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And these are people living in groups or, you know, different kinds of circumstances.
sentences.zh: 这些人生活在群体中，或者，你知道，不同的环境中。

sentences.en: But in the conditions in which we evolved,
sentences.zh: 但在我们进化的条件下，

sentences.en: ethologists and anthropologists had made systematic observations about their power structures.
sentences.zh: 动物行为学家和人类学家对他们的权力结构进行了系统的观察。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So you drop into a group of people in the Amazon or in New Guinea or parts of Indonesia.

sentences.zh: 说到最近新闻里的其他事情，我们目睹了两位亿万富翁因为有钱而被送入太空。

sentences.zh: 那么，那仅仅是在炫耀权力吗？

sentences.zh: 那意味着什么？

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，

sentences.en: I'm sure that this is probably an unfair question because there's so much we don't know.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定这可能是一个不公平的问题，因为我们不知道的事情太多了。

sentences.en: But if you had your druthers, I mean, what are you looking at now?
sentences.zh: 但如果让你选择，我的意思是，你现在在关注什么？

sentences.en: What would you like us to know more about?
sentences.zh: 你希望我们更多地了解什么？

sentences.en: One question is the, and you've already gotten to a part of it, is the trajectory question or the dynamics over time.
sentences.zh: 一个问题是，你已经触及了其中的一部分，即轨迹问题或随时间的动态变化。

sentences.en: I'm regrettably in the United States, we have a lot of stability and immobility in our economic class where we tend,
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，在美国，我们的经济阶层有很大的稳定性和僵化性，我们倾向于，

sentences.en: it's changed where we aren't as mobile as we used to think we were, but there are people who rise in power.
sentences.zh: 情况已经改变，我们不像以前认为的那样具有流动性，但确实有人崛起掌握了权力。

sentences.en: And so there's this interesting question of like, do I abuse power if I rise from a lower class background?
sentences.zh: 所以有一个有趣的问题，比如，如果我从底层背景崛起，我会滥用权力吗？

sentences.en: And now I'm Bill Clinton versus I'm born into privilege and I have power, right?
sentences.zh: 我现在是Bill Clinton，而不是出生在特权阶层并拥有权力，对吧？

sentences.en: So there's this interesting, does that change things that we don't know?
sentences.zh: 所以有一个有趣的问题，这会改变我们不知道的事情吗？

sentences.en: Rising to power versus it coming to you because of your context of birth.
sentences.zh: 崛起掌握权力与因为出身背景而获得权力。

sentences.en: So that's an interesting question.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个有趣的问题。

sentences.en: One of the really interesting questions to me is this, how we approach power, right?
sentences.zh: 对我来说，真正有趣的问题之一是这个，我们如何看待权力，对吧？

sentences.en: Do we really hew to this authoritarian Machiavellian view or do we endorse this more collaborative, cooperative view?
sentences.zh: 我们是真的坚持这种威权主义的马基雅维利观点，还是认可这种更协作、更合作的观点？

sentences.en: And you've kind of brought this up.
sentences.zh: 你已经提到了这一点。

sentences.en: And to me, it's interesting to think about what context do we cultivate this, right?
sentences.zh: 对我来说，思考我们在什么环境下培养这种观点很有趣，对吧？

sentences.en: Are there cultural differences?
sentences.zh: 是否存在文化差异？

sentences.en: You know, psychology probably, and, and, you know, social welfare and so forth is probably more collaborative in its approach to power.
sentences.zh: 你知道，心理学可能，以及社会福利等等，在处理权力的方法上可能更具协作性。

sentences.en: You move over to finance and there's going to be a little bit more coercive approach to power.
sentences.zh: 如果你转向金融领域，那里的权力方法会更具强制性。

sentences.en: So where did the theories of power originate?
sentences.zh: 那么，权力理论起源于哪里呢？

sentences.en: And you asked me that question earlier, and that's an interesting cultural question, right?
sentences.zh: 你之前问过我这个问题，这是一个很有趣的文化问题，对吧？

sentences.en: So I would point to those two questions as needing answers soon.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这两个问题都需要尽快得到解答。

sentences.en: Well, this has been really interesting.
sentences.zh: 好的，这次谈话真的很有意思。

sentences.en: I very much appreciate you taking the time to, to talk to us.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您抽出时间来接受我们的采访。
